patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient has been experiencing progressive left leg pain for 2 months, with recent interference with sleep. The pain was initially treated as 'growing pains' with ibuprofen, without improvement. He recalls being hit in the thigh by a baseball one week before the onset of symptoms, resulting in redness and swelling that lasted several days.

Secondary_Symptoms: History of trauma to the leg

patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: No fever, weight loss, or other systemic symptoms reported.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with progressive left leg pain and assess the pathological causes.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve had progressive pain in my left leg for about two months, and it’s been keeping me up at night. It started after I got hit in the thigh with a baseball, and the area was red and swollen for a few days.
How old are you, and have you noticed any lump
I’m 13, and I haven’t noticed any lump on my left thigh—just the pain that’s been getting worse over time.
Does the pain get better if you take medications like ibuprofen or aspirin?
Patient: No, it hasn’t gotten better with ibuprofen—I tried it at first thinking it was growing pains, but the pain kept worsening. I haven’t taken aspirin for it.
Have you had any fevers, unexplained weight loss, or night sweats recently?
Patient: No, I haven’t had any fevers, weight loss, or night sweats. I’ve just been dealing with the worsening left leg pain and trouble sleeping.
Can you point to exactly where on your thigh the pain

Patient: The pain is on my left thigh, kind of in the middle to upper part of the leg, and it feels deeper than the skin rather than just on one small spot. It seems to get worse when I try to put weight on it or move around.
Have you noticed any redness, warmth, or swelling in

I’ve noticed some redness and warmth around the time it started right after I got hit, and there was swelling for a few days, but it’s mainly the deeper pain now. I don’t feel like it’s swollen the same way anymore, just very painful.

“I think so—the pain has been getting worse and it hasn’t really improved with ibuprofen, and it’s been messing with my sleep. I’m not sure if it’s usually relieved, but right now it doesn’t feel any better after medication.”
Can you describe the pain? Is it a dull
“It feels more like a deep, dull aching pain that can be sharp when I put weight on it or move. It’s been steadily getting worse over the past two months and doesn’t really ease up with ibuprofen.”
Have you had an X-ray or any other imaging
Patient: No, I haven’t had any X-ray or other imaging yet. The pain has just been gradually worsening since the baseball hit, and it’s been starting to really affect my sleep.

Patient: I don’t think I’ve had any recent infections, and nobody else has said I might be sick—just the leg pain started after the baseball hit.
Have you noticed any weakness in your leg
I don’t feel weak in my left leg exactly, but it’s really painful when I try to put weight on it or move, so I end up moving less. I’m able to walk, but I’m limping because of the pain.

“No, I haven’t felt fatigued or sick—just the worsening deep pain in my left thigh and it’s been disrupting my sleep. I can walk, but I limp because it hurts more when I put weight on it or move.”
